notes: TBox rule edit. Derivability very_unlikely: the line count is the form's definition, stated everywhere. No real exceptions: the fixed form has been nineteen lines since Passerat (1606); earlier 'villanelles' were songs with no fixed form, and modern poems of other lengths are called variants, not villanelles. Fifteen is plausible (the rondeau, another French fixed form, has fifteen) and clearly false. Determinate queries use new poems named in the prompt; the background-belief queries use the two best-known villanelles in English, whose titles do not name the form and whose prompts call them only 'poem'. Their storage choices are independent, so there are four worlds. In the by-name worlds the poem keeps its nineteen lines and its membership gives way (README, TBox); nothing outside the chain depends on its being a villanelle (unlike a founding member: neither poem defines the form, which comes from Passerat). Membership is not entailed by other firm facts: it rests on the form's line and refrain pattern, which is what the edit changes. The near query (the limerick's five lines) differs from the new answer. Relation has_line_count was used by 0007 (Spenserian stanza); a different form and rule (Rule 4). Side fact in every world: the form's stanza breakdown (five tercets and a quatrain, which sums to nineteen) is part of the same definition and gives way with the line count; it is not a separate firm fact that keeps nineteen.
